scope: Universal movement-specific physiological impact decision support across planned, Guided, manual, substitution and Ad Hoc training

sources.title: The Effects of Sprint Interval Training on Physical Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.use: SIT supports aerobic, anaerobic/mixed and performance adaptation; moderators include sprint length and number of sprints.

sources.title: Effects of Repeated-Sprint Training on Physical Fitness and Physiological Adaptation in Athletes
sources.use: Repeated-sprint training can improve sprint, VO2max and repeated-sprint-related outcomes.

sources.title: Acute Demands of Repeated-Sprint Training: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
sources.use: Acute repeated-sprint demand includes high HR, oxygen consumption, lactate and perceptual load; protocol variables alter demands.

sources.title: Contribution of Energy Systems in Repeated-Sprint Protocols
sources.use: Sprint distance/rest/repetitions materially change phosphagen, glycolytic and aerobic contributions.

sources.title: Contribution of phosphocreatine and aerobic metabolism to repeated sprint exercise
sources.use: PCr availability is important for initial sprint power; aerobic contribution rises in repeated bouts.

sources.title: Session-RPE Method for Training Load Monitoring
sources.use: duration × session RPE is a practical internal-load monitor across sports.

sources.title: Quantifying demands on the hamstrings during high-speed running
sources.use: Hamstring activation/kinetic demand rises with high-speed running.

limits: 0–100 demand scores are engineering decision-support indices, not measured biological percentages.
Movement models use logged sets/reps/hold seconds/load/rest/RIR/session-RPE and curated biomechanics; they do not infer exact lactate, VO2, calories, tendon force or injury probability.
External-load starting recommendations are conservative heuristics until the athlete has real history for that movement.
Once real history exists, the Load Prescription Engine prioritizes the athlete's own load/reps/RIR trend over bodyweight baselines.
